answer: Every station stamps its own punch pattern into the ticket, and the gate counts the punches against the day's sales. A bridge ticket punched with a copied die fails the gate: the pattern must match the station's own punch at the orchard of the ticket, and a copied die leaves its burrs on the edge. Buying a false punch costs 8,200 in bribes to the ticket clerk and a forged die, and the fable count at the gate is read each evening, so a ticket whose punch was never issued is torn up on the spot.
